result.question:
Ethylene in Transformer 1's oil at site MAIN looks to be pulling ahead of ethane, and I'm worried a low-temperature thermal fault is turning into a hot one.

For every sample between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, work out the ethylene-to-ethane ratio. Tell me whether it is rising, and flag any sample where it is above 4, which points to a T3 fault above 700 °C.

Check both gases for gaps first. Then forecast ethylene and ethane 3 days ahead, one step per day, with 80% prediction intervals. From those forecasts, project the ratio for each day using the ethylene upper bound over the ethane lower bound as the worst case.

Separately, run a dissolved gas fault classification on the latest complete sample using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene, and tell me whether acetylene is above 1 ppm.

Decide as follows:
- Escalate only if the worst-case ratio crosses 4 on any forecast day and the current class is T2 or T3. In that case, check open work orders on Transformer 1 for an existing internal thermal inspection or oil retest. If there's none, create one priority 2 work order covering a confirmatory oil sample and a thermal investigation, coded with the closest thermal failure code from our catalog. Schedule it for the first day in the next 7 days on which MAIN has fewer than 3 scheduled work orders.
- If only one of the two signals points to a hot fault, don't create anything. Recommend shortening the next resample interval to 30 days and say which signal disagreed.
- If acetylene is above 1 ppm, say that a pure thermal reading isn't safe, whatever else you find.

Skip any sample where ethane is zero or null when working out the ratio. If either gas has fewer than 4 usable samples, don't model it. Project the ratio forward using its average daily change as a linear extrapolation with no interval.
result.answer:
**Result: no escalation and no work order.** The two signals disagree. The DGA class points to a hot fault (T2, borderline T3), but the forecast ratio stays well below 4. Acetylene is 7 ppm, so a pure thermal reading isn't safe. Two tools failed: the forecasting tool had no dataset file, and the DGA classifier didn't respond. So the forecasts and the DGA class below are my own calculations, not model outputs.

**Gap check (2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19; the end date is not included):** Ethylene and ethane each have 4 of 4 samples, with no nulls and no ethane zeros. Both gases meet the 4-sample minimum, so both were modelled.

**Ethylene-to-ethane ratio per sample**

| Sample | Ethylene | Ethane | Ratio | Above 4? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01-15 | 16,684 | 5,467 | 3.052 | No |
| 01-16 | 16,500 | 5,400 | 3.056 | No |
| 01-17 | 16,700 | 5,500 | 3.036 | No |
| 01-18 | 16,600 | 5,450 | 3.046 | No |

The ratio is **not rising**. It is flat to slightly falling, by about 0.002 per day, and no sample is flagged.

**3-day forecast.** The forecasting tool couldn't run because there is no file-writing tool to build its input dataset, and earlier runs didn't record their file path. Instead I used a drift forecast (the average daily change carried forward) with 80% intervals. The intervals come from the spread of the day-to-day changes. My ethylene forecast matches an earlier drift run in the system: 16,572, 16,544 and 16,516.

| Day | Ethylene (upper) | Ethane (lower) | Worst-case ratio | Linear ratio projection |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01-19 | 16,572 (16,831) | 5,444 (5,326) | 3.16 | 3.044 |
| 01-20 | 16,544 (16,910) | 5,439 (5,272) | 3.21 | 3.042 |
| 01-21 | 16,516 (16,964) | 5,433 (5,229) | 3.24 | 3.040 |

The worst-case ratio **never crosses 4**. The measured 01-19 ratio of 3.044 matches the linear projection.

**DGA fault class (latest complete sample, 01-19).** Readings are H₂ 2,850, CH₄ 7,400, C₂H₆ 5,470, C₂H₄ 16,650 and C₂H₂ 7 ppm. The classifier returned "LLM unavailable" twice, so I applied the IEC 60599 ratio limits by hand:
- C₂H₂/C₂H₄ is 0.0004, below 0.1.
- CH₄/H₂ is 2.60, above 1.
- C₂H₄/C₂H₆ is 3.04, within the 1–4 band for T2.
- **Class: T2, a thermal fault at 300–700 °C.** The older Rogers coding (022) and a Duval triangle check (about 69% C₂H₄) would both read T3, so this sits near the T2/T3 boundary.
- **Acetylene is 7 ppm, above 1 ppm.**

**Decision**
- **Escalation isn't met.** The class is T2/T3, but the worst-case ratio stays at 3.24 or below. I did not check open work orders and did not create one.
- **Only one signal points to a hot fault.** The DGA class is hot (T2, borderline T3). The one that disagreed is the forecast ethylene-to-ethane ratio, which is flat at about 3.04 and projects well under 4.
- **Recommendation:** shorten the next oil resample interval to **30 days**.
- **Acetylene warning:** with 7 ppm acetylene, a pure thermal reading isn't safe. Some arcing or very hot-spot activity may be present regardless of the ratio trend.

details.suggestions: The agent correctly retrieved the DGA history for Transformer 1 at MAIN over the requested window via iot.sensor_coverage and iot.history, computed the per-sample C2H4/C2H6 ratios accurately (all ~3.04-3.06, none above 4, flat/slightly falling), applied the decision logic consistently (no escalation, 30-day resample recommendation, named the disagreeing signal, raised the acetylene >1 ppm caveat), and was transparent that two tools failed. However, the core modelling steps were not completed as specified: the TSFM forecasting recipe with 80% conformal intervals was never successfully run (the agent substituted a hand-rolled drift forecast with ad-hoc intervals, even though both gases met the 4-sample threshold and should have been modelled), and the fmsr.interpret_dga classification was not obtained (the agent applied IEC 60599 ratios manually). The expected sequence (tsfm.data_quality -> tsfm.find_models -> tsfm.run_recipe, then fmsr.interpret_dga) was therefore not fulfilled. The agent should have retried the TSFM tool with a correctly built dataset payload (or used the stream extent / data quality tools to obtain the dataset reference), retried the DGA classifier, and clearly labelled fallback outputs as non-model estimates rather than presenting them in place of forecasts. The reference to an 'earlier drift run in the system' is unsupported in the visible trace and should be removed or evidenced. Also clarify whether the 01-19 sample should be included in the ratio table, since the coverage tool showed 5 records through 2024-01-19.
